title: 第九节论其他关系和习惯的作用

content.value:
不管前面的论证表现出多么令人信服，我们决不能满足于此，而是必须从每一个方面去探究这一论题，以便发现一些新的论点，据此我们可以南明和证实那样一些奇特的和基本的原理。
在接受任何新的假说时保持一种谨慎的犹豫是哲学家们值得称费的品质，而且对应当遵守的其理加以考察是非常必要的，同时它要求举出可以使他们满意的每一种论证，并且清除能够阻正他们进行推理的每一种反驳。
我多次说过，除了原因和结果以外，类似和接近这两种关系也应当看作是思想的结合原理，并且着作是能够使想象由一个观念移至另一个观念。我也曾经说过，当由这些关系中的任意一种关系所联系的两个对象中的一个直接皇现于记忆或感管的时候，
不仅通过联结原理使心灵传送到与之相关的对象中，而且通过那个原理和这个当下印象的联合作用还使得心灵以一种附加的力量和活力去设想那个相关的对象。我说的所有这些，都是为了通
219—

analogy, my explication of our judgments concerming cause and
effect. But this very argument may, perhaps, be tum’' d against me,
and instead of a confirmation of my hypothesis, may become an objec-
tion to it. For it may be said, that if all the parts of that hypothesis be
true,viz. that these three species of relation are deriv'd from the
same principles; that their effects in inforcing and inlivening our ideas
are the same; and that belief is nothing but a more forcible and vivid
conception of an idea; it shou’ d follow, that that action of the mind
may not only be deriv'd from the relation of cause and effect, but al-
so from those of contiguity and resemblance. But as we find by experi-
ence, that belief arises only from causation, and that we can draw no
inference from one object to another, except they be connected by this
relation, we may conclude, that there is some error in that reasoning,
which leads us into such difficulties.
This is the objection; let us now consider its solution. ' Tis evi-
dent, that whatever is present to the memory, striking upon the mind
with a vivacity, which resembles an immediate impression, must be-
come of considerable moment in all the operations of the mind, and
must easily distinguish itself above the mere fictions of the imagina-
tion. Of these impressions or ideas of the memory we form a kind of
system, compreheniding whatever we remember to have been present,
either to our intermal perception or senses; and every particular of that
system join' d, to the present impressions, we are pleas’ d to call a
reality. But the mind stops not here.For finding, that with this system
of perceptions, there is another connected by custom, or if you will,
by the relation of cause or effect, it proceeds to the consideration of
their ideas; and as it feels that‘′tis in a manner necessarily determin′d
to view these particular ideas, and that the custom or relation, by
which it is determin′ d, admits not of the least change, it forms them
into a new system, which it likewise dignifies with the tile of real-
ities. The first of these systems is the object of the memory and senses;
the second-of the judgment.
—220—

过类比来证实我们关于原因和结果判断的说明。但是，这种恰当的论证或许可以被用来反对我，它可能不是对我的假说的证实，
反而会成为对它的反驳。因为人们或许会说，如果那些假说的所有部分都是正确的，也即：如果这三种关系都是源自于相同的原理，如果它们在加强和活跃我们的观念方面都具有相同的作用，
如果信念仅仅是对一个观念的更为有力和更生动的构想，那么接下来的就应当是：那种心理活动可能不仅仅是源自于因果关系，
而且还源自于接近关系和类似关系。但是，既然我们通过经验已经发现，信念仅仅起源于因果关系，并且发现我们不能从一个对象推到另一个对象，除非它们被这种关系联系着，我们就可以断定，在那种导致我们陷入如此困难的推理中存在一些错误。
这就是反驳；让我们现在来考虑它的解决方法。显而易见，
无论什么呈现于记忆中，并且以类似于一个直接印象的活泼性刺激心灵时，它都必定会在心灵的所有作用中占有相当重要的地位，并且很容易将它自己和单纯在想象中的虚构区分开来。我们将这些印象或记忆观念形成一个系统，其中包括了我们记得的所有呈现于我们的内在知觉或感官的东西；我们将那个系统的每个部分和当下的印象的结合称之为一个实在物。但是，心灵并没有在这重停住。因为它发现，习惯一一如果你愿意，你可以称之为因果关系一将这个知觉系统和另一个知觉系统联系了起来，这样心灵就进而去考虑它们的观念；并且由于它感觉到在某种方式上它必然被决定了去观察这些特殊的观念，而且它被决定所依赖的这些习惯或关系不容许有丝毫改变，所以它把它们形成了新的系统，这个系统同样被它称为实在物。第一个系统是记忆和感官的对象，第二个系统是判断的对象。
—221—

Tis this latter principle which peoples the world, and brings us
acquainted with such existences, as by their removal in time and
place , lie beyond the reach of the senses and memory. By means of it
I paint the universe in my imagination, and fix my attention on any
part of it I please. I form an idea of ROME, which I neither see nor
remember; but which is connected with such impressions as I remem-
ber to have received from the conversation and books of travellers and
historians. This idea of Rome I place in a certain situation on the idea
of an object, which I call the globe. I join to it the conception of a
particular government, and religion, and manners. I look backward
and consider its first foundation; its several revolutions， successes,
and misfortunes. All this, and every thing else, which I believe, are
nothing but ideas; tho'by their force and settled order, arising from
custom and the relation of cause and effect, they distinguish them
selves from the other ideas, which are merely the offspring of the i-
magination.
As to the influence of contiguity and resemblance, we may ob-
serve, that if the contiguous and resembling object be comprehended
in this system of realities, there is no doubt but these two relations
will assist that of cause and effect, and infix the related idea with
more force in the imagination. This I shall enlarge upon presently.
Mean while I shall carry my observation a step farther, and assert,
that even where the related object is but feign' d, the relation will
serve to enliven the idea, and encrease its influence. A poet， no
doubt, will be the better able to form a strong, description of the Ely-
sian fields, that he prompts his imagination by the view of a beautiful
meadow or garden; as at another time he may by his fancy place him
self in the midst of these fabulous regions, that by the feign’ d conti-
guity he may enliven his imagination.
But tho′ I cannot altogether exclude the relations of resemblance
and contiguity from operating on the fancy in this manner, 'tis ob-
servable that, when single, their influence is very feeble and un-
certain. As the relation of cause and effect is requisite to persuade
—222—

后一个原理使我们熟知了那些由于不在时空中因而为我们的记忆和感管所不及的存在物，并且使这些存在物充实于世界之中。通过这个原理，我在我的想象中描绘出宇宙，并且将我的注意固定在我所乐意的任何一部分上面。我形成-一个罗马的观念，
虽然我既没有见到过也没有记起过罗马，但是它却同我所记得的从旅行家们和历史学家的谈话和著述中获取的那些印象联系着。
我将这个罗马的观念置放在我称之为地球的那个对象的观念的某个位置上。我将一个特殊的政府、宗教和风俗的概念附加到这一观念之上。我回溯过去，并且思考它创立之初的情景，思考它的数次革命、成功和不幸。我所相信的所有这些以及其他的种种事物，都仅仅是一些观念；不过通过它们的源自于习惯和因果关系的力量和固定次序，它们都能将自已和仅仅是想象的产物的其他观念区分开来。
至于接近关系和类似关系的影响，我们可以说，如果这种接近和类似的对象被包含在这个实在物的系统中，那么，这两种关系无疑将会帮助因果关系，并且在想象中给这个相关观念注人更多的力量。这一点我马上就要详加阐述。同时，我还将进一步地宣称：即使相关的对象只是捏造的，这种关系也会使那个观念活泼起来，并且增加它的影响。毫无疑问，一个诗人通过对美丽的草地或花园的景色的想象，更容易形成一幅关于乐土的生动的描述；正如在另一个时候他可以通过他的想象将他自己置身于这些神话领域中，从而通过这种捏造的接近关系来活跃他的想象一样。
但是，尽管我不能完全将类似和接近关系排除于想象在这种方式中所起的作用之外，可是我们可以看到，当这两种关系单独出现时，它们的影响是相当微弱和不确定的。正如因果关系对
—223—

us of any real existence, so is this persuasion requisite to give force to
these other relations. For where upon the appearance of an impression
we not only feign another object, but likewise arbitrarily, and of our
mere good-will and pleasure give it a particular relation to the impres-
sion, this can have but a small effect upon the mind; nor is there any
reason, why, upon the retum of the same impression, we shou' d be
determin′ d to place the same object in the same relation to it. There
is no manner of necessity for the mind to feign any resembling and
contiguous objects; and if it feigns such, there is as little necessity for
it always to confine itself to the same, without any difference or varia-
tion. And indeed such a fiction is founded on so lite reason, that
nothing but pure caprice can determine the mind to form it; and that
principle being fluctuating and uncerfain,’ tis impossible it can ever
operate with any considerable degree of force and constancy. The mind
forsees and anticipates the change; and even from the very first in-
stant feels the looseness of its actions, and the weak hold it has of its
objects. And as this imperfection is very sensible in every single in-
stance, it still encreases by experience and observation, when we
compare the several instances we may remember, and form a general
rule against the reposing any assurance in those momentary glimpses
of light, which arise in the imagination from a feign' d resemblance
and contiguity.
The relation of cause and effect has all the opposite advantages.
The objects it presents are fixt and unalterable. The impressions of
the memory never change in any considerable degree; and each im-
pression draws along with it a precise idea, which takes its place in
the imagination, as something solid and real, certain and invariable.
The thought is always determin’ d to pass from the impresion to the i-
dea, and from that particular impression to that particular idea, with-
out any choice or hesitation.
But not content with removing this objection, I shall endeavour to
extract from it a proof of the present doctrine. Contiguity and resemblance

使我们相信任何真实的存在来说是必需的，所以这种信念对给予那些其他的关系以力量来说也是必需的。因为，当一个印象出现时，如果我们不仅捏造出另一个对象，而且还任意地、随已所愿地使这个对象和那个印象发生着一种特殊的关系，那么这个对象对心灵就只有微弱的影响；并且当这个印象在此出现时，也没有任何理由决定我将同一个对象放置在它的同一关系之中。对心灵而言，根本没有必要去捏造任何类似的和接近的对象；而且即使它捏造了这样的对象，它也没有必要总是将它自己限定于这个对象，而没有任何的差异或改变。并且确实，这样一个虚构很少以理性为基础，以至除了纯粹的任性以外，没有什么能决定心灵去形成这种捏造；而且这种任性原则是变化而不确定的，所以它的作用就永远不可能有任何相当程度的力度和恒常性。心灵预见到了这种变化；甚至从一开始就感觉到了它的活动的松散，以及把握它的对象的不牢固。在每个单一的例子中，这个缺点就很明显，而通过实验和观察，它就更为增强了。因为在这里我们可以比较我们能够记起的各个例子，并且形成一条基本的原则：不能将任何信任建立在那些根据捏造的类似和接近关系而在想象中产生的浮光掠影之上。
因果关系却有与之相反的所有的优点。在记忆中呈现的对象是确定而不可改变的。记忆的印象总是没有任何重大程度的改变；并且每个印象都伴随着一个精确的观念，这个观念作为一种坚固的、真实的、确定的和不可改变的东西发生在想象中。思想总是被决定为由印象移至观念，并由那个特殊的印象移至那个特殊的观念，不容有任何的选择或犹豫。
但是，我并不满足于消除这种反驳，我将努力从这个反驳中
—225—

have an effect much inferior to causation; but still have some effect,
and augment the conviction of any opinion, and the vivacity of any
conception. If this can be prov’ d in several new instances, beside
what we have already observ' d,' twill be allow’ d no inconsiderable
argument, that belief is nothing but a lively idea related to a present
impression.
To begin with contiguity; it has been remark' d among the Maho-
metans as well as Christians, that those pilgrims, who have seen
MECCA or the HOLY LAND are ever after more faithful and zealous
believers, than those who have not had that advantage. A man, whose
memory presents him with a lively image of the Red-Sea, and The
Desert, and Jerusalem, and Galilee, can never doubt of any miracu-
lous events, which are related either by Moses or the Euangelists. The
lively idea of the places passes by an easy transition to the facts,
which are suppos’ d to have been related to them by contiguity , and
encreases the belief by encreasing the vivacity of the conception. The
remembrance of these fields and rivers has the same influence on the
vulgar as a new argument; and from the same causes.
We may form a like observation concerming resemblance. We
have remark′ d, that the conclusion, which we draw from a present ob-
ject to its absent cause or effect, is never founded on any qualities,
which we observe in that object, consider′ d in itself; or, in other
words, that‘tis impossible to determine, otherwise than by experience,
what will result from any phaenomenon, or what has preceded it. But
tho′ this be so evident in itself, that it seem′ d not to require any
proof; yet some philosophers have imagin′ d that there is an apparent
cause for the communication of motion, and that a reasonable man
might immediately infer the motion of one body from the impulse of an-
other, without having recouse to any past observation. That this opinion is
—226

去获取一个对当下这个学说的证明。接近关系和类似关系的作用要比因果关系的作用更小，但是它们仍然有某种作用，而且增加了任何意见的确信和任何概念的活泼性。如果在我们已经说过的几个例子之外再有几个新的例子能够证明这种说法，那么这将是信念仅仅是一个于当下印象相关的活泼的观念这个说法的一个相当重要的论证。
先从接近关系谈起；基督教徒和伊斯兰教徒都曾经谈及过，
到过麦加和圣地的朝圣者，在之后要比那些没有这种优势的人更能成为虔诚和热忧的信徒。一个人的记忆如果呈现出红海、沙漠、耶路撒冷和加利利！的生动的意象，他就决不会怀疑与摩西或《福音书》作者们相关的任何神奇的事件。关于这些地方的生动的观念能很容易地移至到那些被假定为由于接近关系而与它们关联的事实上，并且由于增加了这一概念的活泼性而使信念得以增加。对这些田野和河流的记忆对普通人来说具有一个新的论证同样的影响，并且源自于同样的原因。
我们可以对类似关系作同样的考察。我们已经谈及过，我们从一个当下的对象推出它的不在场的原因和结果的那个结论，决不是建立在我们对那个对象的任何性质的观察基础上的，或者换向话说，我们不可能比经验更能断定某种现象将产生什么结果，
或在它之前发生了什么。但是，尽管这一点本身就是如此的明显，以至它看起来好像不需要任何证明，然而有些哲学家却设想：
运动的传达有一个显然的原因，而一个有理性的人无需求助任何
（1）加利利：以色列北部的一个地区，在巴勒斯坦最北部和以色列的古王国，为基督教徒的中心。
—227—

false will admit of an easy proof. For if such an inference may be
drawn merely from the ideas of body, of motion, and of impulse, it
must amount to a demonstration, and must imply the absolute impos-
sibility of any contrary supposition. Every effect, then, beside the
communication of motion, implies a formal contradiction: and’tis im-
possible not only that it can exist, but also that it can be conceiv′ d.
But we may soon satisfy ourselves of the contrary, by forming a clear
and consistent idea of one body′ s moving upon another, and of its
rest immediately upon the contact; or of its returning back in the same
line, in which it came; or of its annihilation; or circular or elliptical
motion: and in short, of an infinite number of other changes, which
we may suppose it to undergo. These suppositions are all consistent
and natural; and the reason, why we imagine the communication of
motion to be more consistent and natural not only than those supposi-
tions, but also than any other natural effect, is founded on the rela-
tion of resemblance betwixt the cause and effect, which is here united
to experience, and binds the objects in the closest and most intimate
manner to each other, so as to make us imagine them to be absolutely
inseparable. Resemblance, then, has the same or a parallel influence
with experience; and as the only immediate effct of experience is to
associate our ideas together, it follows, that all belief arises from the
association of ideas, according to my hypothesis.
Tis universally allow' d by the writers on optics, that the eye
at all times sees an equal number of physical points, and that a
man on the top of a mountain has no larger an image presented to
his senses, that when he is cooped up in the narrowest court or
chamber. 'Tis only by experience that he infers the greatness of the
object from some peculiar qualities of the image; and this inference
of the judgment he confounds with sensation, as is common on oth-
er occasions. Now’ tis evident, that the inference of the judgment

过去的观察的资源，就能马上从一个物体的推动推论出另一个物体的运动来。很容易就能证明这种看法是错误的。因为如果仅仅从物体、运动和推动这三个观念就可以得出这样的推论，那它就必定是确定无疑的，而且必定蕴涵任何相反假定的绝对不可能性。因此，除了运动的传达外，其他任何结果都蕴涵着一种形式上的矛盾：它不仅不可能存在，而且也不可能被设想到。但是我们马上就可以使自已相信相反的说法，因为我们可以形成一个物体进人另一个物体，并且在它们接触时就立即停止的一个清楚和一致的观念，形成物体沿着原来的路线返回的观念，形成物体消灭的观念，形成物体在进行圆形或椭圆形的运动的观念。简而言之，我们可以形成一个可以假定它遭遇到其他无数变化的观念。
这些假定都是一致的和自然的；而我们之所以想象运动的传达要比其他任何假定和自然结果更为一致和自然，其理由就是建立在原因和结果之间的类似关系上；这种类似关系在这里同经验结合起来，并且以最为紧密和密切的方式使这些对象彼此结合在一起，从而使得我们想象它们是完全不可分离的。因此，类似关系就同经验有着相同的或类似的影响；由于经验的唯一直接的作用就是将我们的观念联结在一起，所以接下来的就是：根据我的假说，所有的信念都是源自于观念的联结。
从事光学的作者都会普遍承认，在任何时候，眼晴都会看到相同数目的物理点，而且一个人站在山顶上，其感官所皇现出来的意象也并不比他困在一个最狭窄的庭院或房子里所呈现出来的更大。仅仅是根据经验，他才能从意象的一些特殊的性质推论出物体的大小；他将这种判断的推论和感觉混淆起来，正如在其他场合中经常发生的一样。显然，判断的推论在这里要比我们通一229一

is here much more lively than what is usual in our common reason
ings, and that a man has a more vivid conception of the vast extent of
the ocean from the image he receives by the eye, when he stands on
the top of the high promontory, than merely from hearing the roaring
of the waters. He feels a more sensible pleasure from its magnificence;
which is a proof of a more lively idea: And he confounds his judgment
with sensation;which is another proof of it. But as the inference is e-
qually certain and immediate in both cases, this superior vivacity of
our conception in one case can proceed from nothing but this, that in
drawing an inference from the sight, beside the customary conjunc-
tion, there is also a resemblance betwixt the image and the object we
infer; which strengthens the relation, and conveys the vivacity of the
impression to the related idea with an easier and more natural move-
ment.
No weakness of human nature is more universal and conspicu-
ous than what we commonly call CREDULITY, or a too easy faith in
the testimony of others; and this weakness is also very naturally ac-
counted for from the influence of resemblance. When we receive any
matter of fact upon human testimony, our faith arises from the very
same origin as our inferences from causes to effects, and from effects
to causes; nor is there any thing but our experience of the governing
principles of human nature, which can give us any assurance of the
veracity of men. But tho′ experience be the true standard of this, as
well as of all other judgments, we seldom regulate ourselves entirely
by it; but have a remarkable propensity to believe whatever is repor-
ted，even concerning apparitions, enchantments, and prodigies,
however contrary to daily experience and observation. The words or
discourses of others have an intimate connexion with certain ideas in
their mind; and these ideas have also a conne Vxion with the facts
or objects, which they represent. This latter connexion is generally
much over-rated, and commands our assent beyond what experi-
ence will justify; which can proceed from nothing beside the re-
semblance betwixt the ideas and the facts. Other effects only point

常推理中的所有情形更为活泼；当一个人站在高耸的海角的顶端的时候，根据他的眼睛所获取的意象，要比他仅仅听到海水的啦哮声的时候，对大海的广阔有一个更生动的概念。他从海洋的壮观景象中感到了一种更亲切的愉悦，这就是他有一个更加活泼的观念的证明。同时他又混淆了他的判断和感觉，这又是有一个更加活泼的观念的证明。但是，既然在这两种情况下推论都是同样确定和直接的，那么之所以在前一种情形我们的想象有更大的活泼性，其原因就只能是发生下面的情形：在根据视觉进行推论的时候，除了习惯性的联结以外，在意象和我们推论的对象之间还有一种类似性。这种类似性加强了那种关系，并且通过一种更为容易和更自然的运动把印象的活泼性传送给这个相关的观念。
人性中没有任何弱点比我们通常称之为轻信（也即对别人的证词太容易就相信）更为普遍和显著的了。这一弱点也可以根据类似关系的影响而很自然地加以说明。当我们根据人的证词而接受任何事实时，我们对它的信念就同我们从原因到结果，或从结果到原因的推论一样，产生于相同的根源；而且除了我们的经验以外，再也没有任何东西能给予我们对人的诚实可靠产生任何信任的关于人性的指导原则。但是，尽管经验是这一方面和所有其他判断的真正标准，可是我们却很少完全用这个标准来指导我们自己；而是有一种相信所有传闻的显著倾向，哪怕是一些关于鬼怪、魔术、神奇并与日常的经验和观察相违背的传闻。别人的言辞和谈论同他们心中的某些观念有一种亲密的联系，这些观念又同它们所表象的事实或对象有一种联系。后一种联系又通常被过高地估计，并且强令我们同意不能为经验证实的东西。这种情况只能发生于观念和事实之间的类似关系。其他的结果仅仅

既然类似关系和因果关系在相结合时能增强我们的推理，所以如果在很大程度上缺少了类似关系，也可以几乎完全摧毁我们的推理。关于这一点，一个显著的例子就是人们对来世的普遍不关心和愚钝，它们在这里表现出如此顽固地不信任，正如他们在其他场合表现出如此盲目地轻信一样。没有什么比看到大多数的人们对他们来世情形的疏忽而令勤学的人感到惊奇、令虔诚的人感到遗憾的了；许多杰出的神学家毫不犹豫地断言：尽管普通人没有无神论的理论原理，但是它们在其心中却都是真正的无神论者，并且没有我们像称之为灵魂不朽这样的信仰。这样的断言是有道理的，因为我们可以一方面考虑神学家对不朽的重要性表现出了怎样的口才，同时也可以反省到，虽然在修辞方面我们应当把夸大其词容纳在其中，可是我们即使对不朽进行最有力地描述，也还是无限地低于这一论题。在认识到这一点以后，让我们从另一个方面去观察人们对这个是如何的泰然自若。我要问：这些人们是否会真正地相信他们被教导的、并且为他们自称是肯定了的东西？这个答案显然是否定的。既然信念是源自于习惯的一种心理活动，所以这种说法，也即缺少了类似关系就会推翻习惯所建立的作用，并且正如习惯原则增加它的力量一样减弱观念的力量，就并不奇怪。来世的情形远不是我们所能理解的，而且我们对身体分解后我们的存在方式只有非常含糊不清的观念，所以我们能够创设的所有理由一—不管这些理由是怎样的有力，也不一233一
